title: Micro-unit affordable housing and parkland strategy
subtitle: Also: Kitchener 2051 growth approach, Trussler Road and Sandra Springs changes, Mooregate private street name
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee recommended approval of an affordable rental building at 132 Fairway Road North, made up of small studio and one-bedroom units. Neighbours spoke against it, citing property values, privacy, traffic, noise and parking. Staff said the building is below the height allowed under current zoning and that a site plan application is still to come.

The committee also recommended planning changes for 468 Trussler Road and the Sandra Springs subdivision, and it acknowledged the private street name Mooregate Way. It backed the preferred growth approach for Kitchener 2051 to inform the draft new Official Plan, which staff plan to bring to Council in 2026.

On parkland, the committee recommended that staff develop a Parkland Acquisition Strategy and report back before March 31, 2026. It added a direction to map government-owned properties in each ward by the end of 2025. A second proposed amendment, on funding options including a special tax, was defeated {{vote:m7}}. These are recommendations, and Council will make the final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the Official Plan and zoning changes for a 26-unit affordable multiple dwelling and endorsing the revised urban design brief for the later site plan process.

The committee recommended that staff develop the strategy and report back before March 31, 2026, and identify government-owned properties of interest in each ward and share the data with Council before the end of 2025.
The committee recommended that the preferred approach to growth be used to inform the draft new Official Plan.

The committee recommended modifying the draft plan conditions and approving the Official Plan and zoning amendments, removing the minimum distance separation requirement tied to a nearby equestrian establishment and adding notice and air conditioning conditions.
The committee recommended changing the Block 1 land use from Mixed Use to Low Rise Residential and the zoning from MIX-1 to RES-5.
The committee acknowledged the Region's intended name for the private street at 15-105 Mooregate Crescent and directed Legal Services to proceed with the naming by-law.

debate: Neighbours opposed to the Fairway Road North project raised concerns about property values, privacy from windows and the third-floor terrace, traffic, noise, parking and construction. Some said the area needs family-oriented housing. One delegate said the area already has a lot of low-income housing.

Supporters on the committee said the project offers a new entry point for people on low incomes, pointing to people living in tents or shared rooms. They noted that staff had cut windows on the side facing the neighbour and that the building is lower than current zoning allows.

Questions about the Fairway project focused on the small unit size, laundry and storage, rents, and how tenants would be chosen. One councillor noted that the one-bedroom rents exceed the 30%-of-minimum-wage affordability measure. The applicant said agency referrals and an income test would be used.
Staff warned that refusing the Fairway project could lead to an appeal to the Ontario Land Tribunal, where they said approvals are common, and that Council could face costs.
On parkland, one councillor said school-board open spaces should count toward local provision, while others said these spaces are not parks. Staff said the strategy would not rely on them.

The councillor who proposed the parkland amendments said earlier 2022 directions were still unfinished and that land in critical areas may disappear. Staff and others said a funding report needed the full analysis and the first quarter of 2026. The mapping amendment passed once it was clarified as mapping only.
